title: PlateWasteEvent
description: Emitted by a plate-waste sensor (simulated camera+scale stand-in today; real vendor integration, e.g. Winnow webhook, later). Represents a single bussed-plate observation.

event_id.description: Unique identifier for this event, assigned by the producer.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema, e.g. '1.0.0'. Consumers must reject unknown major versions. 1.1.0 added the optional edge_inference object; events without it remain valid 1.0.0 events. 1.2.0 added the optional edge_inference.shift_score; events without it remain valid 1.1.0 events. 1.3.0 added the optional edge_inference.flatline_score; events without it remain valid 1.2.0 events.

source_id.description: Identifier of the emitting device/adapter, e.g. 'sim-plate-cam-03' or 'winnow-adapter-01'.

source_kind.description: Distinguishes stand-in producers from future real integrations without changing the contract. 'player' (added 2026-09-20) marks a human-driven source, for example an interactive client.

table_id.description: Originating table, if traceable. Null if untraceable (e.g. batch bussing).

plate_item_ids.description: Menu item IDs believed present on the plate. Empty array permitted if unresolved.

confounder_flags.description: Known confounding signals captured at observation time, so downstream causal inference is not forced to infer them. Not a claim of dissatisfaction.

image_ref.description: Optional MinIO object key for a reference image. Null when no imaging stand-in is used.

edge_inference.description: Present (schema 1.1.0 and later) when estimated_waste_grams was produced by a model running on the node itself, from raw sensor channels, instead of being reported by a vendor system. Describes that model and the node's own assessment of whether to trust the estimate. Absent for sources that do no on-node inference.

model_sha256.description: SHA-256 over everything that determines the model's behaviour (weights, input statistics, guard calibration). Lets any stored estimate be tied to the exact model that produced it.

inference_latency_ms.description: Wall-clock time the node spent computing this estimate.

ood_score.description: Mahalanobis distance of this reading's sensor channels from the model's training data. Large means the inputs look unlike anything the model was trained on.

out_of_distribution.description: True when ood_score exceeds the threshold calibrated on held-out data. Estimates flagged true are excluded from causal analysis.

drift_score.description: Rolling mean of squared ood_score over the node's last window of readings. Null until the window has filled (for example just after a restart).

shift_score.description: Hotelling T-squared of the mean deviation of the sensor channels from the training data over the node's last shift window of readings (schema 1.2.0 and later). Near the number of channels when the inputs look like the training data; a sustained bias in any direction (for example a fouled lens) raises it. Null until the window has filled.

flatline_score.description: The smallest per-channel standard deviation over the node's last flatline window of readings, in units of the training spread (schema 1.3.0 and later). Around 0.9 on clean data; a sensor stuck at a plausible value, or a gain that has fallen, drags it toward 0. An alarm is a score BELOW the calibrated threshold. Null until the window has filled, and always null for a model from before the flatline monitor.

drift_suspected.description: True when drift_score or shift_score exceeds its calibrated threshold, or flatline_score falls below its own: a sustained change in the sensor inputs even though no single reading is anomalous (for example a fouled lens, or a sensor stuck at a normal value). drift_score reacts to added spread, shift_score to a consistent bias, flatline_score to a channel that has stopped varying. False while all are null.
